rationale: The raw winner model favors Menifield because of 17 UFC bouts, deeper late-fight evidence, and a reach edge.
Iwo's three UFC wins all ended in Round 1 and his entire UFC sample is only 3:22, so the winner model heavily penalizes uncertainty.
The conditional method model strongly favors KO if Iwo wins: 75.4% baseline and 67.0% shadow; the largest joint outcome is Iwo KO at 34.8%.
Menifield has been knocked out by Carlos Ulberg and Azamat Murzakanov, so the power path is not theoretical.
Iwo is 27, 9-0, has seven KO wins and two submissions, a judo base, and every professional win has come in Round 1.
Menifield's best path is surviving the opening storm, using his 3-inch reach advantage and experience, and forcing Iwo into minutes and rounds he has never shown as a professional.
Because Iwo's sample is extremely short, the research lean should not be converted into a high numeric probability or used to justify an expensive favorite price.
